To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a new parametrization of leptonic mixing matrix has been developed in which deviations from maximal atmospheric and zero reactor mixing are obtained from charged lepton sector corrections, which is able to reduce the number of phases, thus, simplify the analysis.
the deviations of reactor mixing and atmospheric mixing angles can be obtained in terms of charged lepton corrections.

the parametrization of lepton mixing in terms of charged lepton corrections allows to obtain relatively large deviations of the reactor angle from zero, and the Jarlskog CP violating phase can be identified as the Dirac phase.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the parametrization of lepton mixing matrix and the CP violation.
a parametrization in which the deviations of lepton mixing matrix from the tribimaximal mixing is obtained from corrections from charged lepton sector, and in which there are fewer complex phases.
the parametrization of lepton mixing matrix and the CP violation in neutrino sector.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the charged lepton corrections to the mixing matrix can explain the deviations of the reactor mixing angle and the atmospheric mixing angle from their maximal values.

the charged lepton corrections to the lepton mixing angles are not only possible but also natural and can explain the deviations from maximal mixing in atmospheric sector as well as the vanishing reactor mixing.
the parametrization in terms of charged lepton corrections is very useful for the analysis of the lepton sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the deviations from maximal mixing and vanishing mixing can be parametrized in terms of small charged lepton corrections.
the deviations for the reactor angle from zero can be obtained from the corrections in the charged lepton mass matrix and the Jarlskog CP violating measure can be obtained in terms of single phase.

we have obtained a parametrization for the lepton mixing in which the deviations of the atmospheric mixing from maximal and the reactor mixing from zero are obtained in terms charged lepton corrections and a Dirac-type CP phase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the parametrization of neutrino mixing in terms of charged lepton corrections is a viable alternative to the standard parametrization in terms of neutrino mass and mixing angles.
the deviations from the maximal atmospheric mixing and reactor mixing angles can be explained in terms of the corrections from the charged leptons.
the charged lepton corrections can play an important role in understanding the lepton mixing pattern.
